# Install Profiler — a switchable DSH skill plugin

A DeepSeek Harness **bundle** that registers one model-invocable skill,
`install-profiler`, in the p

rofile-global skill layer. It teaches the agent to
turn a Windows installer (or an installed applica

tion) into an evidence-backed
map — install paths, registry writes, services, config files, logs, Ev

ent Log
sources — and then diagnose install/startup/runtime faults with a
symptom→cause→mechanism→fi

sources — and then diagnose install/startup/runtime faults with a
symptom→cause→mechanism→fix chain.

Part of the **DSH plugins** index: <https://github.com/MLMLZJ/dsh-plugins>
Companion plugin: <https:

//github.com/MLMLZJ/dsh-reverse-skill> (decompilation;
consumes the `handoff.md` this plugin produce

ithub.com/MLMLZJ/dsh-reverse-skill> (decompilation;
consumes the `handoff.md` this plugin produces).

Disable the row (or the whole bundle) in Plugin Manager and the skill disappears
from the session ca

talog; enable it again and it comes back, re-reading
`SKILL.md` so edits apply without restarting Ha

`SKILL.md` so edits apply without restarting Harness.
## What it does

- **Static profiling, no execution.** Classifies MSI / NSIS / Inno Setup /
InstallShield / WiX Burn

/ Squirrel / Electron / MSIX / SFX packages, then
extracts the payload and reads the install definit

ion.
- **MSI is read as a database.** `export-msi-tables.ps1` drives the built-in
`WindowsInstaller.

Installer` COM server — no lessmsi needed — and emits
`profile.json` plus one CSV per table (`Direct

ory`, `File`, `Registry`,
`ServiceInstall`, `ServiceControl`, `Shortcut`, `Environment`, `CustomActi

on`,
`InstallExecuteSequence`, `LaunchCondition`, `Upgrade`, …).
- **Runtime state, read-only.** `co

llect-state.ps1` gathers uninstall entries,
live services (with binary existence), drivers, startup

items, scheduled
tasks, Event Log source registrations, app data/log dirs, WER crash folders,
MSI lo

gs and pending-reboot flags, and flags concrete anomalies.
- **Fault playbook.** `references/fault-p

laybook.md` carries the MSI error-code
table, the service-startup triage order, crash evidence sourc

es, the
upgrade/repair/uninstall failure matrix, and how to read a before/after diff —
with the mech
anism behind each one.
## Where this stops and reverse-engineering starts
The two skills are complementary, not overlapping:
- **`install-profiler`** answers *what should be observed* — install layout, registry, services, log

s, event sources, and which of them to watch at runtime.
- **`reverse-engineering`** answers *how to
read the code* — .NET (`ilspycmd`), Electron (`asar`), native (`objdump`/`rizin`/Ghidra).
When an installer is itself a .NET bootstrap or an Electron/Squirrel app and strings are not enough,
`build-handoff.ps1` packages the handoff: it classifies the branch (dotnet / electron / pyinstaller
/ native / packed), lists the facts already established, turns the gaps into branch-specific questi
ons, emits the exact decompile commands with tool availability, and writes `handoff.md` + `handoff.j
son`. The receiving skill is told not to redo discovery and to tag every answer `[verified]/[inferre
iving skill is told not to redo discovery and to tag every answer `[verified]/[inferred]/[unknown]`.
`mine-strings.ps1` covers the common case without needing any decompiler; its output is evidence of
capability, not proof of behaviour.
## The loop: static map → dynamic probe

Static facts say what *should* happen; the fault is in what *actually* happens.
The profile is the a
iming device, not the deliverable:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

`build-probe-plan` resolves MSI directory roots to real machine paths, lists the
registry keys worth

snapshotting (ARP, services, EventLog, Run, COM), states each
service's expected start type/account

against its live state, names the process
names and config/log candidates, emits Event Log provider

s/IDs and Procmon filter
expressions, and produces a check list with the command and expectation for

each.
It also writes **`ops-card.md`** — a one-page, copy-pasteable sheet for whoever is
fixing the

machine: where everything is, the triage order, and the exact commands
for layout, process, log tai
l, crash events, service config, ports and uninstall.

MSI packages feed it `-Profile`. Portable, PyInstaller and Electron apps have no
MSI: feed it `-AppD

ir` plus the `collect-state` / `mine-strings` output, and the
plan is built from real machine paths
and runtime-discovered directories instead.

`diff-snapshots` ranks what moved: files added/removed/modified under watched
paths, registry values

created/changed/deleted, service state changes, processes
appearing/exiting, ports opening/closing,

new Event Log entries, new WER crash
folders.
## Scripts
| Script | Purpose |

| `scripts/probe-tools.ps1` | Which extractor/inspector tools exist (read-only, ~2 s) |
| `scripts/d

etect-installer.ps1` | Classify the package + emit the extraction plan |
| `scripts/mine-strings.ps1
` | No MSI database? Mine registry paths, log paths, services, URLs, GUIDs and error templates out o

f the binary (ASCII + UTF-16LE) |
| `scripts/build-handoff.ps1` | Package the evidence into a paste-
ready brief for the reverse-engineering skill: branch, established facts, questions, commands, evide

nce contract |
| `scripts/build-ops-sheet.ps1` | Assemble the complete operations sheet: every unins
tall value, full service registry keys, all startup entries, every log/config file, event sources, M

SI registry rows + triage commands |
| `scripts/watch-process.ps1` | Sample a process over time to p

rove CPU/thread/handle/memory leaks and name the threads that consume CPU |
| `scripts/export-msi-ta

bles.ps1` | MSI tables → JSON/CSV + derived profile |
| `scripts/collect-state.ps1` | Read-only runt

ime snapshot for an installed app |
| `scripts/build-probe-plan.ps1` | Static profile → targeted dyn

amic-observation plan |
| `scripts/capture-snapshot.ps1` | Execute the plan: files, registry, servic

es, processes, ports, events |
| `scripts/diff-snapshots.ps1` | Before/after diff → ranked findings
with mechanism hints |

Invoke with `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File <path> …`
(Windows blocks local scr

rshell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File <path> …`
(Windows blocks local scripts by default).
